transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Lena Park (Aperture VP Product), Ravi Singh (Aperture ML Eng), Tom Anders (Aperture Procurement), Sara Holt (Aperture Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Agreed on a 6-week POC with a credits allocation; focus on note summarization and reranker latency/accuracy.
- Bench plan: three workloads (real-time summarization, batched embeddings, reranking) with throughput and token cost targets.
- Procurement: SOW -> PO; security review required.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do quick intros, then scope the pilot and cover credits and procurement path, sound good?
[00:06] Lena Park: yes, thanks maya, i'm lena, vp product, i'll be leading the success criteria side.
[00:11] Ravi Singh: ravi here, ml eng, i'll run the dataset prep and the bench runs with you.
[00:16] Tom Anders: tom, procurement, i'll help route the PO and contract side.
[00:19] Sara Holt: sara, security, i'll flag any compliance asks.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: diego, se at redwood, i'll own the bench harness and perf configs.
[00:26] Maya Chen: cool. quick context — aperture is evaluating for clinical note summarization and an internal reranking workload, correct?
[00:33] Lena Park: correct. two main use cases: extractive/abstractive summaries for clinician triage and a reranker for existing search results.
[00:40] Maya Chen: and current stack? what are you running today for inference?
[00:43] Ravi Singh: mostly on-prem huggingface endpoints right now, some gpu clusters via our infra team; throughput is poor and costs are spiky. we do a lot of batch jobs overnight but clinicians want sub-500ms median for live summaries.
[00:56] Diego Alvarez: okay that latency target is helpful — we're used to tuning for sub-300 to sub-600ms depending on model size and seq length. what's your typical context window/seq length?
[01:05] Ravi Singh: average notes are 1,200 tokens after tokenization, but the useful context is typically the last 512 tokens. embedding calls for patient similarity are 512 tokens, reranker inputs average 256 tokens.
[01:18] Maya Chen: good — that helps size the workloads. for the pilot we usually define three bench profiles: realtime low-latency gen, batch embedding throughput, and reranking latency + quality. does that match?
[01:27] Lena Park: yes. our success criteria are: summaries hit >85% clinician-accepted rate on a 200-case blind eval, median latency <500ms for live path, and 90th percentile cost per 1k tokens below our internal threshold — we'll share that number.
[01:41] Diego Alvarez: excellent. high level pilot mechanics — we propose a 6-week pilot: 1 week setup/ingest, 2 weeks benching, 2 weeks integration checks with clinicians, 1 week wrap + results and exec review. credits-wise, we're proposing 40k compute credits for the POC — that typically covers the bench run plus integration for this scope.
[01:58] Tom Anders: can you explain what 40k credits maps to in dollars or token units? procurement needs mapping to budget.
[02:04] Maya Chen: yeah, we can map. rough math — with our hosted pricing typical equivalence is about $0.xx per 1k tokens depending on model; but credits are an internal abstraction. we'll include a conversion table in the quote. for transparency we can also show a sample bench spreadsheet with estimated token burn per workload.
[02:20] Ravi Singh: we need to know if those credits can be consumed across model variants or if there's a locked model for the pilot.
[02:25] Diego Alvarez: flexible — we recommend starting on a mid-sized open model to hit latency and then test a quantized variant. credits cover usage across model choices but we'll flag higher-cost variants in the report.
[02:36] Sara Holt: on security — what's in scope for the pilot in terms of data residency, encryption, and audit logs? we have PHI so need strong controls.
[02:43] Priya Rao: hopefully this part's ok to hear, priya from cs. for hosted pilots we offer encryption in transit and at rest, KMS integration for Private deployments, and detailed audit logs. for customers who need on-prem we offer a private deployment option but that requires enterprise conversations.
[02:58] Sara Holt: do you have SOC2 and iso docs?
[03:01] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC2 Type II, iso certifications, and a security packet we'll send — includes KMS notes, retention, and redaction best practices.
[03:09] Tom Anders: procurement — what paperwork do you need? we prefer PO + SOW, do you accept short-term pilots via a simple agreement?
[03:16] Maya Chen: for pilots we can do a statement of work (SOW) + a purchase order; small pilots often use a short pilot addendum to the SOW. we'll provide a template.
[03:24] Tom Anders: timing… we'd need about 2-3 weeks for internal approvals after we sign. is that a blocker?
[03:30] Maya Chen: we can align — pilot start can be gated on PO but we can spin up the bench environment earlier with sample data if you want to fast-follow.
[03:38] Ravi Singh: i'd like to get the bench harness running so we can baseline current perf vs redwood. what are the standard bench scripts?
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: we'll supply a harness that runs multi-profiles: fixed-rps latency tests, burst tests, and token burn accounting. common configs — 50 concurrent requests for reranker, 10 rps for live summarization, batch embedding jobs sized at ~5k records to measure throughput.
[04:00] Lena Park: can we set guardrails on spend? e.g., hard cap that stops the pilot if credits nearing exhaustion?
[04:05] Maya Chen: absolutely — we can set hard ceilings and alerting; the console shows token consumption and credits left. we'll also add a notification to the AE and your procurement contact at 80% usage.
[04:14] Priya Rao: i'll set up a dedicated trial account with role-based access so only bench owners can run tests.
[04:19] Ravi Singh: about success metrics — besides clinician acceptance and latency, we also want to see regression tests for hallucination rates. is that feasible in the bench?
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can include prompt sets and golden references to compute precision/recall-like metrics and an automated hallucination check — though the latter is heuristic.
[04:34] Lena Park: what's the path to production if pilot looks good — do we need a dedicated pool?
[04:38] Maya Chen: typically next steps are: agree on SLA and committed capacity (dedicated) or continue hosted with reserved throughput. dedicated gives predictable latency and lower unit costs for sustained load. we'll provide pricing scenarios for both.
[04:50] Tom Anders: pricing scenarios and a commercial timeline would help me forecast. include lead times for dedicated capacity.
[04:55] Maya Chen: noted. dedicated lead time depends on region and GPU availability; typical ramp is 4-8 weeks after contract. we'll include a conservative timeline.
[05:03] Ravi Singh: for the bench we'll need to instrument token-level cost outputs, also KV cache behavior was mentioned earlier — does redwood keep warm KV cache during bench?
[05:12] Diego Alvarez: yes, bench can emulate warm KV cache but we'll show both cold/warm paths. that affects latency a lot, so we'll capture both median and p95.
[05:20] Sara Holt: about data — we will not share PHI unless we have a DPA and proper encryption in place. can you sign a DPA?
[05:26] Maya Chen: yes, we have a template DPA; we'll include that with the security packet. for initial bench you can share de-identified samples.
[05:33] Lena Park: sample size for evaluation — we plan a 200-case blind clinician eval; benchmark dataset should be 1k-2k records to capture variance.
[05:41] Diego Alvarez: recommended: 1k bench records for embeddings throughput, 500 for reranking sweeps, 200 for live latency sampling; that'll give statistically meaningful numbers.
[05:50] Ravi Singh: what's the expected token burn for those sizes? rough estimate?
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: rough: embeddings 1k * 512 tokens each ~512k tokens; reranker 500 * 256 * (assume 3 candidates) approx 384k tokens; live gen 200 * 600 tokens ~120k tokens; plus overhead — so total ~1.1M tokens. we'll map tokens to credits in quote.
[06:12] Maya Chen: so that aligns with our 40k credit suggestion — but we'll show both conservative and aggressive scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[06:20] Lena Park: ok. on success criteria, we'll define thresholds and a go/no-go matrix for the exec review.
[06:26] Maya Chen: good. procurement path recap: we send SOW + pilot addendum and pilot quote. you raise PO against that SOW. security gets the packet and signs DPA. pilot activated on PO receipt or earlier with a sandbox if you want to start benching pre-PO.
[06:40] Tom Anders: any contract length requirements after pilot? we don't want to be locked in.
[06:44] Maya Chen: no lock-in for pilots; enterprise commitments are separate. we'll offer a conversion credit if you sign a committed capacity within X days — we'll outline that.
[06:54] Priya Rao: one more ops question — will we be able to switch models mid-pilot for regression testing?
[06:59] Diego Alvarez: yes, you can test model variants; we'll tag runs so cost and latency by model are clear.
[07:04] Lena Park: what about support during pilot — SE hours?
[07:07] Maya Chen: included: weekly sync + 8 SE hours included for bench setup; additional hours billed or covered under enterprise support. we'll detail that.
[07:15] Ravi Singh: ok let's talk milestone dates: if quote goes out on 2/13 and PO by 2/24, pilot could start first week of march?
[07:22] Maya Chen: yeah that's feasible — setup week of 3/3, bench 3/10-3/23, integration 3/24-4/4, wrap 4/7. that's a 6-week window.
[07:32] Tom Anders: internal approvals likely complete 2/24, i'll try to expedite.
[07:35] Sara Holt: security can start reviewing the packet as soon as you send it.
[07:38] Maya Chen: perfect. recap and next steps — i'll summarize: send pilot quote with 40k credits and conversion table, attach SOW template and DPA, diego will share bench harness and sample configs, and aperture to send de-identified samples. we'll schedule the benchmark week once samples and PO are aligned.
[07:56] Lena Park: sounds good. any other blockers?
[07:59] Ravi Singh: none from me.
[08:01] Tom Anders: none, thanks.
[08:03] Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email and put next sync on calendar.

End of call.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attribution and filler words present; product names occasionally spelled with spaces (K V cache) or hyphenation.
